documents.generated_document: HOSPITAL: Apex Medical Center | DEPARTMENT: Cardiology Clinic | PATIENT NAME: Robert Jenkins | MRN: 9938271 | DOB: 04/12/1951 | AGE: 72 | SEX: Male | ENCOUNTER DATE: 10/24/2023 | DOCUMENT TYPE: Progress Note | PROVIDER: Dr. Sarah Lin, MD *** CHIEF COMPLAINT: Worsening shortness of breath and palpitations. *** HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: Mr. Jenkins is a 72-year-old established patient with a history of HFrEF (LVEF 35%), CAD, and CKD stage 3 who presents today with a 3-day history of progressively worsening dyspnea on exertion, orthopnea requiring 3 pillows, and new-onset palpitations. He reports an 8-pound weight gain over the past week despite adherence to his home dose of oral furosemide. He denies frank chest pain, syncope, or fever. *** REVIEW OF SYSTEMS: Cardiovascular: Positive for palpitations, orthopnea, and leg swelling. Negative for chest pain. Respiratory: Positive for shortness of breath. All other systems reviewed and are negative. *** PHYSICAL EXAMINATION: VITAL SIGNS: BP 105/65, HR 118 (irregularly irregular), RR 22, Temp 98.6 F, SpO2 91% on room air. GENERAL: Mild respiratory distress, speaking in short sentences. CV: Tachycardic, irregularly irregular rhythm. No murmurs. JVD present to the angle of the jaw. RESP: Crackles noted in bilateral lower bases. EXT: 2+ pitting edema to the mid-calves bilaterally. *** DATA REVIEWED: 1. In-office EKG performed today: Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, rate 118 bpm. No acute ST-T wave changes. (Independent interpretation by me). 2. Stat POC BMP: Creatinine 1.9 (baseline 1.5), K 4.0. 3. Stat POC BNP: 1450 pg/mL. *** ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: 1. Acute on chronic systolic heart failure exacerbation: High severity. The patient is fluid overloaded with hypoxia. Administered Furosemide 80 mg IV push in the clinic today with good initial urine output. 2. New-onset Atrial Fibrillation with RVR: High risk. Discussed the need for direct admission to the hospital for rate control and diuresis. The patient adamantly refuses hospital admission at this time due to family reasons. We will attempt aggressive outpatient management. Increased Carvedilol to 12.5 mg BID. Continuing Apixaban for stroke prophylaxis. 3. Acute Kidney Injury on CKD: Likely cardiorenal syndrome. Will monitor closely. PLAN: Patient will return to the clinic tomorrow morning for a recheck of his weight, vitals, and renal function. Strict return precautions given for ER if symptoms worsen. *** Electronically Signed By: Dr. Sarah Lin, MD | Date Signed: 10/24/2023 15:30 | End of Report
